source.title: A Differential Topological View of Challenges in Learning with Feedforward Neural Networks

record.file_problem: None; the supplied text contains the full paper.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own experiment on how activation-function slope affects generalization, a conceptual test of V6's broad concern with conditions that change test performance. It does not test the listed dropout claim itself.
record.gate_note: The only reported result bearing directly on a mapped version is the toy experiment varying sigmoid slope and comparing learned curves with ground truth. The paper's width/depth, optimization, and regularization claims outside that experiment are theoretical arguments or cited prior work, not separate empirical results.
record.test_reason: The study tests activation-slope and representation-architecture effects on toy function-learning tasks, which match none of V1–V8. Its discussion of generalization without explicit regularization does not test V1's random-label versus natural-label comparison. V6 specifically concerns dropout, which is not manipulated.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the authors' generalization argument: activation-function slope provides implicit regularization, and their toy experiment qualitatively suggests poorer generalization with larger slopes. Their overall conclusion is broader: differential topology offers a framework for studying expressibility, optimization, generalization, and architecture.
record.recipe_differences: The empirical work uses toy function-learning and representation tasks with batch learning, backpropagation or an approximate Newton method, and sigmoid activations; it does not reproduce the claim versions' experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The toy function-learning result varies the sigmoid parameter a ∈ {1, 5, 10}; the paper reports generalization decreases as maximal slope increases.

fits_no_version.finding: For F(2,10,10,2) learning a circle-to-figure-eight map from 51 perturbed samples, Figure 2 qualitatively suggests poorer generalization as sigmoid parameter a increases from 1 to 5 to 10.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing sigmoid slope can worsen qualitative generalization in this toy function-learning setting.

fits_no_version.finding: On 1000 held-out Swiss-roll samples, F(3,10,10,10,2) slightly outperforms F(3,10,10,1,10,2) in prediction-error mean, variance, and tail; the authors attribute the difference to bottleneck training difficulty.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: An information-lossless architecture can slightly outperform a deeper narrow-bottleneck architecture on this toy mapping task.

record.problems: The main generalization experiment is a toy function-learning task, and reports only a qualitative comparison of curves without numerical test errors or uncertainty. The representation experiment uses one stated train/test setup and presents exact error distributions only in a figure.
record.rows_left_out: No results omitted. The theoretical discussion and cited studies were not entered as empirical rows.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and chance-level held-out performance compared with natural-label generalization under the same architecture and recipe.
Test-error behavior as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity or initialization.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD, including tuning, weight decay, and optimizer switching.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove their penalty.
Dropout effects, training-set-size dependence, excessive dropout, and joint removal with weight decay.
Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation sharpness, its association with generalization gaps, and comparisons with other measures.
Removing highly memorized training examples versus removing random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The record's tests/T2 classification is inconsistent with its correctly unmapped rows. Shared interest in generalization does not make an activation-slope experiment a test of the dropout claim. Row states indicate inability to assess V1–V8, not absence of the paper's qualitative findings.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label test generalization coexistence.
Whether test error keeps falling as one-hidden-layer ReLU networks widen past interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classification generalization.
Generalization comparisons between adaptive optimizers and SGD.
Large-batch training and its dependence on epoch budget or recipe.
Dropout's effect, training-set-size dependence, and removal alongside weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relationship to the generalization gap.
Effect of removing memorized training examples on test accuracy.

rows.subject: three-layer DNN F(2, 10, 10, 2)
rows.operation_detail: Trained to learn the map from a unit circle to a two-petal rose while varying parameterized sigmoid slope.
rows.measure: Qualitative learned-curve generalization against ground truth; text describes performance as better at lower maximal slope.
rows.value: Figure 2(a) depicts the learned curve for a = 1; no numerical test error is stated.
rows.note: Toy function-learning experiment, not classification with dropout or the held-out natural-label behavior in the listed versions.
rows.check: Valid unrelated result, but it cannot establish any listed version. Parameter a controls sigmoid slope; the actual maximum derivative is a/4.
